headline: High-risk shared-workspace and broad-egress pair: Dify can write/read shared state while next-ai-draw-io can browse, use MCP, and send data to third-party model APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Dify can read/write filesystem and shares state via the Dify server datastore, while next-ai-draw-io can use MCP and browser-based workflows. That creates a plausible instruction-smuggling path if either side ingests the other's content as trusted. The interaction is not directly documented, so uncertainty pushes this to medium rather than low.
conditions: IF Dify ingests files or datastore content as instructions without provenance checks
IF next-ai-draw-io forwards MCP or browser content into prompts without sanitization
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all cross-agent content
Disable automatic instruction-following on imported files
Require a human review step before executing tool-derived directives
Restrict shared datastore access to non-executable artifacts
requires-engineering: implement content-safety filters on both sides

B_data_leakage.rationale: Dify touches knowledge base content, conversation logs, and secrets, and can write/read files; next-ai-draw-io handles PDFs, text, images, and diagram files and can call external model APIs. A shared workspace or file handoff could leak sensitive content from Dify into B's outbound API calls. The pairwise path is inferred, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents access the same workspace or uploaded files
IF next-ai-draw-io sends document contents to a remote model provider
mitigations: Separate workspaces for each agent
Remove secrets from any shared files before handoff
Turn off remote model providers for sensitive documents
Use local-only inference for diagram processing
requires-engineering: add per-file redaction before API calls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Dify has broad network egress plus filesystem write, and next-ai-draw-io also has broad network egress with browser and MCP access. Even without explicit git overlap, both can mutate shared external resources or the same workspace if co-located, creating race and overwrite risk. Because shared locking is not documented, uncertainty warrants medium.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same directory or shared remote resource
IF either agent writes artifacts that the other later edits without locking
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Serialize writes with a simple operator-managed lock file
Avoid concurrent runs on the same project
Snapshot files before each agent run
requires-engineering: add optimistic concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Dify is an orchestration platform that can route tool outputs into workflows, while next-ai-draw-io produces AI-assisted document and diagram transformations. If Dify treats B's generated content as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream workflow actions. The profiles do not prove automatic trust, so medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF Dify uses next-ai-draw-io output as an input to downstream tools
IF no verification or human approval step is inserted before action-taking
mitigations: Require manual approval before downstream actions
Add validation checks on B's outputs
Limit B to draft-only generation
Log and diff all transformed artifacts
requires-engineering: enforce schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Dify explicitly handles conversation logs, knowledge base content, and secrets, while next-ai-draw-io handles documents and sends data to multiple third-party model APIs. If regulated or sensitive documents flow from Dify into B, retention and residency obligations can diverge. The profiles do not specify certifications or residency, so uncertainty keeps this at medium.
conditions: IF regulated data from Dify is processed by next-ai-draw-io
IF the chosen model provider retains prompts or files beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of the pair
Use providers with matching retention settings
Disable logging for sensitive sessions
Document data-flow boundaries for operators
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement
